target_customer: Young professionals renting rooms and apartments in Latin American city centers, and property owners
problem: City center housing in Latin America was expensive and unmanaged; Viya bundled leases with cleaning, maintenance and laundry.
business_model: Leases of rooms and apartments with bundled services
product_category: Mobile first rental housing and co-living

founders.name: Benjamin Garcia
founders.background_notes: YC profile cites 8 years of VC and PE investing.

founders.name: Francisco Puente
founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A leasing and service operations business with a mobile app; the hard part was operations, not engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Operational execution with leased inventory; no data or network moat evident.

market_need_then: YC page claims about $60k MRR growing 20% weekly for three months with 40% margins, self reported and unverified elsewhere.

branding.domain_note: viyaliving.com now redirects to a HugeDomains sale page, so the domain is for sale.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand coverage found; the domain is now parked for sale.

outcome_analysis: Viya was a Monterrey based Latin American rental and services company with a self reported $60k MRR in early 2020 and a $150K entry attributed to YC and two angels or funds by databases. YC marks it inactive and its domain is now for sale, but no post-mortem, news report or acquisition was found, so the cause of failure is not public. COVID-19 timing is plausible context but no source ties it to Viya.
notes: Round amount rests on CB Insights and Employbl (Diffbot) databases, no date given. Competitor search found no source dated near the batch for LatAm co-living (Casai raised Oct 2020, after the batch and short term focused), so the list is empty. MIT claim comes from the YC profile bio only. The YC page lists 22 team members yet no press was found. Branding search found nothing about Viya Living.
